items.out: You believe the bank will open tomorrow because it opened today. Put your weight on that and notice what it is made of: the authority's silence. A closure of this kind works only if nobody says it is coming, since the saying would be the signal to leave, so the shutting has to land in the hours you are already locked out, the Friday night, the bank holiday, the Sunday address, and by the time you can act the act is forbidden by name. Greece, whose banks did not open on Monday 29 June 2015 after a Sunday television speech; Cyprus in March 2013, a bank holiday stretched, after parliament refused the first levy, until the bail-in was law; Argentina's corralito announced on a Saturday in December 2001; the export licence suspended and the delisting published, both after the fact. What you lose is a permission, the leave to move what is yours. What runs the clock is the authority's calendar, laid deliberately over the hours you are shut out. What could have kept it is a transfer made on rumour, paying the price of being wrong and the discount the rumour market charges, because the deposits that left Greece that spring left on nothing better than that. Here is the drop: this is the one expiry on the map whose notice cannot come first, and if you are waiting for a date you are waiting for a thing the mechanism itself forbids. Runway-illusions' Cash behind glass counts the deposit taken into receivership on a Friday as owned and unreachable; this is the mechanism that chose the Friday. It is not investor-tells' Let it lapse, a fuse the founder can test by letting it pass, since a closure you can probe is not one that must be a surprise; it is not an offer withdrawn or a rival's foreclosure, which someone at your own table decides, since the decree is an authority's rule on a class and nobody at your table decided about you. The item stands on that fence alone, and not on any claim that the exit dies as a side effect, since the decree forbids the exit by name.

items.out: You think that if a claim of yours were about to expire, someone would have told you. Lean on that and it goes. The date was fixed in a room you were not in, in a proceeding you are not attending, and the law says you have read it, because it ran in a newspaper: the bankruptcy court's bar date for proofs of claim, noticed to unknown creditors by publication; the class settlement whose opt-out date arrives on a postcard that looks like advertising; the probate creditor's window that opens and shuts with a notice in the county paper. What you lose is a permission, the standing to be paid, or to sue on your own. What runs the clock is the bar-date order married to the rule of constructive notice, under which publication counts as knowledge for everyone the debtor could not name, which is to say for you. What could have kept it is a one-page proof of claim or a signed opt-out, the cheapest filing in the law and the one least often made, and now see why it is least made: the holder who would file it is, by construction, the one who was not told. The floor was the belief that knowledge comes before the deadline; here the deadline is the thing you are deemed to know. Runway-illusions' Stamp's clock is a permission with a date the holder can read on the stamp; this is that permission with its date written on someone else's docket and imputed to you. Not deal-deaths' Missing witness, because nothing is missing from the record; only you were missing from the room.
items.back: Bar date in the newspaper: the claim expires on a date fixed in a proceeding the holder is not attending and is deemed to have read, since notice ran by publication, as the bankruptcy court's bar date for proofs of claim, noticed to unknown creditors by publication, the class settlement whose opt-out date arrives on a postcard that looks like advertising, and the probate creditor's window that runs from the notice in the county paper; the condition lost is a permission, the standing to be paid or to sue on one's own; the carrier is the bar-date order together with the rule of constructive notice, under which publication counts as knowledge for anyone the debtor could not name; the last intervention that could have kept it is a one-page proof of claim or a signed opt-out, the cheapest filing in the law and the one least often made, since the holder who would make it is by construction the one who was not told; adds to runway-illusions' Stamp's clock, a permission with a date the holder can read on the stamp, the date that is written on someone else's docket and imputed to the holder; not deal-deaths' Missing witness, since nothing is missing from the record, only the holder from the room.

items.out: The grant you hold has no date on it, and you take that for permanence. It is the opposite. It means the date lives on a paper you never signed and may never have read, the parent instrument the grant was issued under, and when the parent's term ends yours ends with it, whatever its own merits. The emergency-use authorization that ends when the declaration it was issued under is terminated, which is a different paper from the public-health emergency that ended in May 2023 and left the authorizations standing; the cross-state telehealth licence that lapsed with each state's emergency through 2021 and 2022; the wartime power; the pilot run under a waiver; the sub-lease that dies with the head lease. What you lose is a permission. What runs the clock is the parent's date, and the first thing you must do, standing where you thought there was floor, is find out which parent paper carries it, since the grant you did read carried none. What could have kept it is conversion, a full approval, a permanent rule, a licence in your own name, filed while the parent still stands, and conversion is slow enough that it has to be started while the emergency looks endless, which is exactly the season in which nobody starts it. Not Bar date in the newspaper, where the date sits on a docket and is imputed to you; here the date is on a different paper than the option and it is honest. Not lead-time-floors' Calendar with nothing in it, a wait the rule imposes; here the rule does not wait, it ends.
items.back: Emergency over: the option was granted under a parent instrument with a term of its own, so it expires when the parent does, whatever its own merits and with no date printed on it, as the emergency-use authorization that ends when the declaration it was issued under is terminated, a different paper from the public-health emergency that ended in May 2023 and left the authorizations standing, the cross-state telehealth licence that lapsed with each state's emergency in 2021 and 2022, the wartime power, the pilot programme run under a waiver, the sub-lease that dies with the head lease; the condition lost is a permission; the carrier is the parent instrument's date, which the holder never signed and may never have read, since the grant it did read carried no date, so the holder must first find which parent paper carries it; the last intervention that could have kept it is conversion, a full approval, a permanent rule, a licence in one's own name, filed while the parent still stands, and the conversion is slow enough that it must be started while the emergency looks endless, which is exactly when nobody starts it; not Bar date in the newspaper, where the date is on a docket and imputed, since here the date is on a different paper than the option and is honest, and not lead-time-floors' Calendar with nothing in it, a wait the rule imposes, since here the rule does not wait but ends.

items.out: You assume the one who holds an option is the one who can save it. Here the holder is a child who does not know she has an eye to save, and the clock is her own cortex, on a schedule she cannot read and nobody outside can read with precision. Amblyopia is most correctable by patching the good eye in the first years and responds less, and less completely, after about seven, though the trials of the 2000s found response into the early teens; the clubfoot cast in infancy; the second language spoken without an accent, which is contested as a hard window; the duckling that imprints in its first day. What is lost is a capability, the cortex's willingness to rewire. What runs the clock is the developmental timetable. What could have kept it is a screening, the preschool vision check, the parent who notices a squint, so the option belongs to one person and its preservation to another, and where no screening programme exists the option expires unseen at a rate that is a property of the programme and not of the child. That is where the ground goes: the count of these expiries is set by an institution the child will never meet. Last known well has a witness dating the option; this is the case where the holder cannot be her own witness at all. It is not a use-it-or-lose-it, since nothing the child does or leaves undone runs the clock.

items.out: You assume the body keeps its own time and medicine reads it. Then you learn the protocol does not ask the tissue when the artery closed; it asks who saw you last. The stroke patient who wakes with the deficit is ineligible for thrombolysis because the four-and-a-half-hour window is counted from when she was last seen well, which was bedtime, so the wake-up stroke loses the drug regardless of when the artery closed. The same rule dates the opened vial with no time written on the label and the sample whose chain of custody has a gap: expired at the earliest moment they could have been. What is lost is a capability, a treatment the protocol now forbids. What runs the clock is the protocol's timestamp rule, which asks for a witness and not for the tissue. What could have kept it is a witness, someone awake, a time written on the vial, or a witness of a different kind, the imaging that reads the tissue's own clock, by which the WAKE-UP trial of 2018 returned the drug to patients with no witnessed onset. The floor was the fact; what you are actually standing on is the record of the fact, and the record runs out first. Witness-architectures asks what must exist for a trace to form; this is the option that dies for want of a trace while the fact would still allow it. Not Patch before seven, where the body's own clock has run; here the body's clock may not have run, and the record's has.

items.out: You assume a question put to a court gets an answer, yes or no. Watch it dissolve under you with neither. The situation resolves itself faster than the forum moves, so nobody declines and nobody rules: the student whose challenge to a law school's admissions was dismissed as moot because he was about to graduate (DeFunis, 1974); the pregnancy over before the appeal; the election held before the ballot-access case; the tenant evicted before the housing court sits; the employee whose grievance is mooted by the reorganization that abolished the post. What is lost is a permission, the justiciability of the claim. What runs the clock is a ratio, the forum's pace over the harm's duration, and no party at the table sets either term. What could have kept it is a structure that outlives the individual harm: the class certified before the named plaintiff's harm ends, which is what Sosna (1975) allowed, or the doctrine that a harm capable of repetition yet evading review may be decided anyway, which is what Roe rested on. So the option is kept by a coordination or by a rule, and never, look down and see it, by hurrying. Not deal-deaths' Cost of the last mile, where the surplus is eaten on a curve; here nothing is eaten and the harm is simply over. Not Bar date in the newspaper; there is no date anywhere.

items.out: You assume a body that has not said no is a body that might still say yes. Then its term ends with your matter pending, and the body that could have said yes is gone, and its successor never has to say no, because it starts you from zero. Bills that die on adjournment sine die and must be reintroduced from the beginning; the treaty signed and waiting on a parliament that is dissolved; the permit application before a council that is re-elected; the approval the old board agreed in the hallway and had not yet minuted when the board was reconstituted at the meeting; the offer approved by a committee that is disbanded in the reorganization. What expires is your place in the process. What is lost is a counterparty, the specific body whose yes was available. What runs the clock is the ratifier's own calendar, its election, its session, its term. What could have kept it is the vote scheduled before adjournment, the carry-over motion, the approval minuted rather than agreed in the hallway. Be honest about the treaty cases: most unratified treaties were eventually refused by someone, so the clean form is the legislative bill, which dies by the thousand each session with no recorded no. Deal-deaths' Ratifier's other deal has a ratifier that wanted a different bargain; this is the ratifier that wanted this one and was gone before the vote. Not Landlord changes, where the counterparty is replaced by a transfer; here it is replaced by the calendar.
items.back: Session ends: the body that could have said yes reaches the end of its own term with the matter pending, and its successor never has to say no, since it starts the matter at zero, as the bills that die on adjournment sine die and must be reintroduced from the beginning, the treaty signed and awaiting a parliament that is dissolved, the permit application before a council that is re-elected, the approval the old board agreed in the hallway and had not yet minuted when the board was reconstituted at the meeting, the offer approved by a committee that is disbanded in the reorganization; what expires is the matter's place in the process; the condition lost is a counterparty, the specific body whose yes was available; the carrier is the ratifier's own calendar, election, session, or term; the last intervention that could have kept it is the vote scheduled before adjournment, the carry-over motion, the approval minuted rather than agreed in the hallway; the treaty cases are simplified, since most unratified treaties were eventually refused by someone, and the clean form is the legislative bill, which dies by the thousand each session with no recorded no; adds to deal-deaths' Ratifier's other deal, where the ratifier wanted a different bargain, the ratifier that wanted this one and was gone before the vote; not Landlord changes, where the counterparty is replaced by transfer, since here it is replaced by the calendar.

items.out: You assume a promise attaches to the thing it is about. It attaches to the person who made it, and that person can be sold out from under you, or leave, or be succeeded, and you often will not see it happen. The renewal promised by the landlord who sells the building to a buyer not bound by unrecorded promises; the 'we'll take you back' from a manager who leaves; the side letter with a fund's partner that the fund's successor manager has never seen; the supplier's verbal priority that vanishes with the account executive. What is lost is a counterparty, the one whose word held the option. What runs the clock is the register, the deed, the fund agreement, the offer letter on letterhead, the paper that transfers, on which your option was never written, so the successor takes free of it. What could have kept it is recording, a memorandum of option on the title, a side letter countersigned by the entity, the promise moved onto the paper that binds successors, at the price of the awkwardness of asking a friendly counterparty to bind their unknown replacement. That awkwardness was the floor you chose not to test. Term-sheet-powers' Successor in the chair has the replacement exercising a term the friend would not have; this is its mirror, the replacement declining to honour a term the friend gave. Not Chair grown over, where the counterparty stays and the shape goes.
items.back: Landlord changes: an option held in a person rather than on the paper that transfers expires at the counterparty's next transfer, which the holder does not control and often does not see, as the renewal promised by the landlord who sells the building to a buyer not bound by unrecorded promises, the 'we'll take you back' from a manager who leaves, the side letter with a fund's partner that the fund's successor manager has never seen, the supplier's verbal priority that vanishes with the account executive; the condition lost is a counterparty, the one whose word held the option; the carrier is the register, the deed, the fund agreement, the offer letter on letterhead, on which the option was never written, so the successor takes free of it; the last intervention that could have kept it is recording, a memorandum of option on the title, a side letter countersigned by the entity, the promise put on the paper that binds successors, which costs the awkwardness of asking a friendly counterparty to bind their unknown replacement; adds to term-sheet-powers' Successor in the chair, where the replacement exercises a term the friend would not have, the mirror case, where the replacement declines to honour a term the friend gave; not Chair grown over, where the counterparty stays and the shape goes.

items.out: You assume a seat you left is a seat that is waiting. Nobody is holding it. It is a vacancy, and a vacancy is only a thing the counterparty has not yet re-planned, and at the next planning cycle it is re-planned, and no one declines your return because no one is asked. The leave taken with no return date whose post is redistributed among three people at the next reorganization; the budget line reallocated at year end; the supplier's line retooled for the customer who stayed; the co-founder's seat the remaining founders stop leaving empty at the next hire. What expires is the return to the seat; employment there afterwards is a new negotiation from the outside. What is lost is a capability on the counterparty's side, the shape that could receive you. What runs the clock is the counterparty's planning cadence, quarterly, annual, the next reorganization, and it sets the expiry without reference to you at all; that is the bottom going, that you were never in the calculation. What could have kept it is a dated return, a leave rather than a resignation, a reservation the cycle must respect, or the return itself before the cycle turns. Traces-of-the-unlived's Vacancy tenant has preparation for a future breeding its opponents; here no one opposes the return and the absence is simply absorbed. Not forms-of-return's Reentry burn, a road open and hostile one way; this road has closed.

items.out: You assume a yes, once given, is yours to keep. Each yes is decaying from the moment it is signed, so an option that needs many yeses at once is a thing with a half-life, and it expires unless your gathering outruns the rot of what you have already gathered. The recall petition whose signatures older than sixty days are invalid under Michigan's rule, or must all fall within California's hundred and sixty days; the tender offer's minimum condition that must be met by the offer's expiry; the crowd in the square that goes home; the reunion that becomes impossible one death at a time. What is lost is a coordination. What runs the clock is the validity window on each act of assent, written by the rule or by the assenter's own attention. What could have kept it is a gathering rate, paid circulators, a date agreed in advance, a pact that binds the early yeses until the last arrives. Say plainly which of these is measured: the recall and tender cases are observed, and the crowd is analogy. Who-can-be-bound's Place in line is an ordering lost by your leaving; this is the coordination lost by others' leaving. Not Session ends, where one body's calendar kills the matter; here many small calendars do, and none of them is the one you were watching.

items.out: You assume that growing makes you more saleable. Every round that raises your price moves the natural buyer further out of reach, until the round that prices you above what the acquirer can pay at all: a market capitalization smaller than the price, a wage cap, a fund's concentration limit, and past those a board's approval ceiling, with nobody at either table declining anything. The company whose preference stack now exceeds the largest deal its three strategic buyers have ever done; the player whose wage outgrows every club in the league but two; the practice too large for any partner to buy in and too small to be listed. What is lost is a counterparty, the buyer whose capacity was the option. What runs the clock is the acquirer's capacity, readable in its market value and its deal history, set against your own price, which each round raises. What could have kept it is the sale at the last price under the ceiling, which was never seen as the last, or a round sized to stay under it, which is the one choice a founder is never advised to make. Look down: the thing you did to be worth more is the thing that removed the buyer. This is analytical, since every observed case can be read as a buyer that would have paid more, so it stands as a mechanism and not a count. Market-deaths' Slowed past the rot has a market thinning from the outside; this is the market for you that you thin by growing. Not Chair grown over, where the counterparty re-plans; here the counterparty is unchanged and you have left its range.

items.out: You assume a permit is a thing you hold. It is a thing you are standing on, and the ground under it is being rewritten by a third party's rule change, and no paper you can file will keep it; only an act in the world will. The building that may proceed under the old zoning only if the developer has substantially begun in reliance on a valid permit before the ordinance passes; the footings poured the week of the council vote; the nonconforming use that survives the new code only if it is in use on the effective date; the grandfathered rate kept only by the account that was open. What is lost is a permission. What runs the clock is the code and the vested-rights doctrine, which in most states vests on construction begun and in a few, as in Washington, on a complete application, so the last act differs by jurisdiction and the holder who knows which has a different week. What could have kept it is the hole in the ground before the vote, an exercise begun rather than a filing made: the option can be preserved only by starting to use it. First-mover-forecloses holds the rival who changes the rules on purpose; this is the rule that changes for reasons of its own. Not Slot flown empty, where the exercise must be repeated to keep the right; here one beginning vests it for good.
items.back: Pour the foundation: a permission is about to be withdrawn by a third party's rule change, and it can be kept only by an act in the world that no paper substitutes for, as the building that may proceed under the old zoning only if the developer has substantially begun in reliance on a valid permit before the ordinance passes, the footings poured the week of the council vote, the nonconforming use that survives the new code only if it is in use on the effective date, the grandfathered rate kept only by the account that was open; the condition lost is a permission; the carrier is the code and the vested-rights doctrine, which in most states vests on construction begun and in a few, as in Washington, on a complete application, so the last act differs by jurisdiction and the holder who knows which has a different week; the last intervention that could have kept it is the hole in the ground before the vote, which is an exercise begun rather than a filing made, so the option can be preserved only by starting to use it; adds to first-mover-forecloses, which holds the rival who changes the rules on purpose, the rule that changes for reasons of its own; not Slot flown empty, where the exercise must be repeated to keep the right, since here one beginning vests it for good.

items.out: You assume that not using a thing is how you keep it. Here the clock runs precisely while you do nothing and stops only when you act, and the act that keeps it is the exercise with its purpose removed. The airport slot that must be flown eighty percent of the season or returned, which had airlines flying empty aircraft in early 2020 until the rule was waived; the water right under prior appropriation, forfeited after five years without beneficial use, which has fields irrigated in a drought to keep them; the trade mark abandoned after three years' non-use; the mining claim kept by annual labour; the department budget spent in the last quarter so that it is not cut. What is lost is a permission. What runs the clock is the regulator's usage ledger. What could have kept it is the empty flight, which costs the whole price of using the option and returns nothing but the option, so that keeping and using are the same act and the option's upkeep is its exercise price. Runway-illusions' Stamp's clock has a licence that lapses without hours logged and that no cash extends; this is the price at which it can be extended after all, the hours flown for nobody. Tollgates-that-must-buy's Stamp with an expiry has a gate that must spend its stamp; this is the permission-holder who must burn the permission to keep it. Power-trades' Leased strike has disuse making a power unbelieved; this is disuse forfeiting it by rule. items.out: You assume you can go back until you decide not to. The way back closes at the first act the new state performs that the old state cannot read, and that act is not a decision about going back at all; it is the new state doing its ordinary work. What is lost is a capability, the old state's ability to take over from here. What runs the clock is the first write, performed by the new state in the ordinary course. So the window is the pause between the change and its first consequence, and the reversibility you thought you were standing on was only ever that pause. What could have kept it is the expand-and-contract shape, writing to both for a season so the old can still read, at the price of running two and of a season in which neither is the truth. Pivot-invariants names the retained assets that make leaving cheap; this is the moment one of them is lost. Undo-costs bills a reversal that remains possible; this is the reversal that stops being possible. Not Thawed to be ready, where readiness spoils the good; here the new state's use closes the way back to the old.

items.out: You assume the thing holding the option open is on the option's side. The device that keeps it open accumulates its own harm with each week it runs, or its lapse is one-way, so the deadline is the machine's and not the situation's. The patient on ECMO as a bridge to transplant who becomes ineligible for the transplant the machine was keeping her alive for, since bleeding, infection, and clotting rise with each week on circuit and centres set a duration beyond which candidacy is reviewed; the mothballed mine kept dry by pumps whose stopping floods the workings past reopening; the ship in the reserve fleet whose hull is kept by cathodic protection that a budget line can end; the interim chief who has run the company past the point where the search can bring in an outsider. What is lost is a capability, the eligibility or the workings. What runs the clock is the bridge itself, its complication rate or its upkeep bill. What could have kept it is a listing at the moment of cannulation, a search begun the day the interim was named, a decision to stop pumping taken while a sale was still possible, each of which treats the bridge's start as the option's deadline, and that is the inversion you have to make while the ground still feels solid: the day the machine went on was the day the clock started. The ECMO limits are centre practice and are simplified. Lead-time-floors' Bridge is a degraded replacement priced by the hour; this is the bridge that ends the option it holds open. Not Standstill with a term, where the clock is a date the counterparty signs; here the clock is a harm nobody signs.

items.out: You assume that pausing keeps things as they were. The pause you took to keep the option open was written on a paper with a date, so a situation that had no deadline now has one, and the paper's renewal belongs to the other side, who now knows what the pause is worth to you. The tolling agreement that stops the limitations clock you could have stopped alone by filing, and that expires in twelve months unless the adversary signs again; the negotiated leave of absence that dates a job which had no date and is extended only if the employer signs; the forbearance agreement that holds the lender's foreclosure for ninety days; the furlough whose recall rights run six months; the standstill in a takeover that keeps the bidder from buying shares and ends on the day it says. What is lost is a permission, the leave to remain in the paused state. What runs the clock is the pause's own instrument, and its clock is the only clock in the situation that you wrote; that is where the floor goes, that the one deadline in the room is the one you put there. What could have kept it is the renewal asked for before the counterparty learns it is needed, or a pause written without a term, which is rarely granted; the Korean armistice is the exception that has no renewal date and is still called temporary. The statutory pauses, the family-leave statute's twelve weeks and the restraining order's fourteen days, are the same date without the mechanism, since the term is a rule's and the renewal belongs to a court or to no one, so the holder gets the deadline without paying the counterparty for it; they are runway-illusions' Stamp's clock. Impasse-inventions' cooling-off right offers reversibility as a chip; this is the bill the chip carries. Not lead-time-floors' No-shop, which serializes the search; here the search is stopped, and the stopping is what expires.
